## BOOK 1 of 2: "The O'Ruddy: A Romance" — Stephen Crane & Robert Barr (Gutenberg 29573, 1903, Frederick A. Stokes Co.)
Narrator: Tom O'Ruddy ("The O'Ruddy"), Irish, of Glandore near the Old Head of Kinsale, Co. Cork. Father (recently dead) gave him papers belonging to young Lord Strepp (later Earl of Westport) and two swords: grand one from King Louis, plain one. Father lent Strepp breeches in France (Strepp's breeches on a bush after a ford). Servants: Mickey Clancy (steward at Glandore), Father Donovan (priest). Ship "Martha Bixby" mentioned.

Ch I: Arrives Bristol; inn (fat landlord, bleating). Supper: garrulous man in plum-colour; Strepp (about 20, fair, ruddy), Colonel Royale (about 40, clear-eyed, soldierly), Forister (dark-skinned, proud). Colonel tells breeches story; O'Ruddy shouts "That, sir, is a lie," gives the lie twice. Waiters bundle him out. Strepp visits; challenge accepted for daybreak; O'Ruddy claims a friend. Forister mocks Irish; O'Ruddy boxes his ear and kicks him through the inn door; Forister crashes into a servant with cloaks/cushions/rugs. Earl of Westport (tall, old eagle-like, black cloak) and two ladies (one with bright eyes, Lady Mary) arrive; O'Ruddy names himself; Earl: "You are your father's son. Come to my chamber in the morning." Bargeman with cold in other hood. Strepp and Royale seen laughing at window.
Ch II: Irish vagabond keening, red-haired "Paddy" (blue velvet, flowered waistcoat, pink stockings, King Louis sword slung on string). Duel at dawn on green turf; Paddy's "lashings" proposal. O'Ruddy laughs in Colonel's face; wounds Royale in four places (sword arm); spares him ("Damme if I will"). Crowd of boys; Paddy's hair. Royale faints; O'Ruddy and Strepp tend him.
Ch III: Papers missing from luggage; O'Ruddy suspects Forister, pursues to Bath; Paddy wins (uses his hat-chase). Highwayman Jem Bottles (7 ballads in Bristol, 3 in Bath; mother Dame Bottles; Susan and eggs, Farmer Hants) robbed at oak tree; O'Ruddy takes his horses, borrows 14 guineas; Bottles' mother.
Ch IV: Thinks of Lady Mary; learns Forister went back to Bristol. Forister found at wayside inn with Bottles' sweetheart; Paddy had barricaded him ("little black man"). 
Ch V: Forister denies papers; "Nell" hint; O'Ruddy goes to Earl's chamber in Bath (Westport, Tompkins valet, Lady Mary; Earl: "worthless... straw"). Earl's 'You are a rascal'; O'Ruddy stands like a stone; Earl accuses him of jewels/theft.
Ch VI: Papers fall from pillow; O'Ruddy gives sword (hilt first) and papers to Lady Mary. Strepp, Royale; Forister is Strepp's father's partner in shipping and family friend; Royale tells of Ponsonby/Stewart duel; O'Ruddy plans to run away; Royale offers port.
Ch VII: O'Ruddy considers abandoning Glandore; decides to fight. Forister visits; Nell, "the child" taunts; Royale arrives.
Ch VIII: Lady Mary's letter/ talk in garden; Countess harangues Parrot ("pretty lady"); Countess ("Hoity-toity") chases O'Ruddy round chairs and table. Lady Mary tells him not to fight Forister ("certain death"); "I did not wish you to suppose... I have paid this debt."
Ch IX: Father's lancer story; Royale's "God spare you!" note from Lady Mary; duel with Forister in Bristol: O'Ruddy wounds Forister in left shoulder; Forister's sword thrown.
Ch X: Famous-swordsman fame; Countess chase again (ivory fan thrown).
Ch XI: Forister carried away; O'Ruddy meets Paddy and Jem Bottles by haycock reading Lady Mary's letter (papers were Earl's carriage papers, robbed by Paddy & Jem on Bristol road; contents of purse 15 guineas). O'Ruddy returns papers to himself; decides to give to Lady Mary.
Ch XII: Bath: Earl's chamber; O'Ruddy claims papers in breast; "Lady Mary Strepp" as true owner; Sir Edmund Flixton; Earl asks why not read papers; O'Ruddy says he'd get a tutor.
Ch XIII: Earl knows of love; Countess and Paddy fight on stairs; Paddy's disguise; Paddy eats like barbarian.
Ch XIV: Paddy holds Countess against wall with chair; O'Ruddy hides under bed then flees; Bath inn.
Ch XV–XVI: Journey to London; Paddy's hard-head philosophy; inn at night in Bristol/Bath area; "Mr. O'Ruddy celebrated Irish swordsman" tale; Jem tested on fencing jargon "sticadoro proderodo sliceriscum"; servants trained (bottles as sword/coat).
Ch XVII–XVIII: London; "Pig and Turnip" inn, Bishopsgate Street; Paddy's hair cut; Mr. Fullbil (critic/wit) at dinner; Bobbs (dramatist), Fancher (critic), Dr. Chord (little scientist, kites). O'Ruddy insults Fullbil ("not in Italy"; Ireland tale).
Ch XIX: Mug-house "Red Slipper" with Paddy and Jem; Jem sings ballad; parrot-like fight.
Ch XX–XXI: Kensington Gardens; Dr. Chord's gossip (Marquis of Stubblington, Lord Gram, Countess Cheer); Lady Mary glance; O'Ruddy's father's Mollie story.
Ch XXII–XXIII: O'Ruddy declares to Chord he'll marry Mary; plan to climb tree into Earl's garden; Chord flees; gardener Strammers with blunderbuss captures O'Ruddy; Lady Mary intervenes; O'Ruddy declares love; "blunderbuss loaded."
Ch XXIV–XXVI: Paddy & Jem befriend Strammers (promise to see gardens); Chord tips papers story; night before Sunday plan.
Ch XXVII: Sunday: Paddy & Jem beaten in Westport gardens; O'Ruddy enters house; locked room with Lady Mary; kiss; papers given to her; she sends him to Mr. Josiah Brooks in the Temple (letter of introduction); "fairest estate... Brede (Sussex)" and five hundred guineas.
Ch XXVIII: O'Ruddy meets Father Donovan in St. Patrick's chapel; Doctor Chord gets ruined by Paddy and Jem (Chord's "medicine").
Ch XXIX–XXX: Brooks (lawyer); O'Ruddy tells him story; attacked by nine ruffians on the street; he takes their nine swords; sends to Brooks; Brooks gives 500 guineas; Father Donovan joins; O'Ruddy and Donovan ride to Rye.
Ch XXXI–XXXII: Paddy & Jem robbed nine men in forest (Dr. Chord among them); Tom Peel (giant smuggler) hired with nine men; occupy Brede House (caretaker; secret tunnel; ghost Sir Goddard Oxenbridge).
Ch XXXIII: Earl's men attack; Strepp captured in tunnel; O'Ruddy releases; Strepp: "King O'Ruddy." Paddy falls through trap-door. Earl's manor conference; Countess slaps O'Ruddy; Lady Mary consents; marriage by Father Donovan. Memoirs end with children: Patrick, Mary, Terence, Kathleen, Michael, Bridget, Donovan.

## BOOK 2 of 2: "The Duke Decides" — Headon Hill (Gutenberg 37413, 1903, A. Wessels Co.)
Frontispiece/illustrations: Leonie Sherman; "A countrywoman of yours. I wonder if you know her?"; "The procession of three led by the stranger."; "I am very far from being indifferent to Mrs. Talmage Eglinton."

Ch I "The Man with the Mandate": May, New York, dry-goods store (Bowery). Charles Hanbury, ex-cavalry subaltern, now $8/week clerk (adds sales-tickets; lamed by hatchway fall). Stout Englishman "Jevons" in Panama hat; bar on Bowery; offers $500 (five $100 notes) for planting forged US Treasury bonds on Bank of England (£3 million). Chief: Clinton Ziegler, Hotel Cecil, London. Telegram: uncle and cousin (George Hanbury) killed in railway accident; Pattisons (solicitors). Hanbury becomes Charles Augustus Trevor Fitzroy Hanbury, 7th Duke of Beaumanoir (£200,000 a year).
Ch II "On Board the St. Paul": Leonie Sherman (daughter of Senator Leonidas Sherman; mother Mrs. Sherman). Marker = spy (brown covert-coat, tweed cap, cabin next door). Southampton arrival.
Ch III "A Task-master in Goggles": Ziegler at Hotel Cecil in invalid chair, blue glasses, white beard; three masked men; "Let him alone"; Ziegler knows of Leonie; instructions: Senator brings bonds; deposit at Bank; return Saturday.
Ch IV "The Lady in the Landau": Alec Forsyth (friend, Eton, Foreign Office clerk); General Sadgrove (uncle, Indian Staff Corps, 140 Grosvenor Gardens); Sybil Hanbury (cousin, 18, orphan, engaged to Alec); Mrs. Talmage Eglinton in landau (invites to tea Saturday; Duke refuses). Duke offers Alec secretary post (£800/yr).
Ch V "Ziegler Begins to Move": Prior's Tarrant (Hertfordshire); vicar Mr. Bristow; butler Manson; lame gardener Jennings lassoed; charcoal brazier in chimney of Duke's Room.
Ch VI "The General is Curious": Sadgrove saw Mrs. Talmage Eglinton's landau knock down Duke; Duke's diachylon-plastered wrist; Senator's bonds sailing on Campania.
Ch VII "The Men on the Stairs": John Street, Adelphi (Alec's rooms); Marker outside; "Rat" password; forced entry; Alec returns; Duke gone.
Ch VIII "The Cut Panel": Beaumanoir House, Piccadilly; butler Prince; fake detective "Inspector Chantrey" (clerical garb); Sybil spots him; Duke's door panel cut with watch-spring saw; Sybil catches intruder.
Ch IX "The Strategy of the General": Azimoolah Khan (Pathan orderly); apple-woman; General plans move to Prior's Tarrant.
Ch X "A Duty Call": General visits Mrs. Talmage Eglinton; Thakore of Bhurtnagur (Azimoolah disguised) raid; she asks when Duke goes; "8.45 from St. Pancras."
Ch XI "On the Terrace": train derailed; Forsyth receives forged telegram from "Sybil"; Duke alone on train; Azimoolah fights.
Ch XII "The Man Under the Seat": Marker under seat; train stopped by baulk of timber near Elstree/Radlett; Duke flees into woods.
Ch XIII "At the Keeper's Cottage": Mayne the keeper (Sir Claude Asprey's); "Colonel Anstruther Walcot" impostor; Duke escapes via woodshed roof; Azimoolah follows.
Ch XIV "Too Many Women": Duke's suspicion; Sybil & General conference; anonymous note scented (same perfume as Mrs. Talmage Eglinton's): "There is danger from Ziegler."
Ch XV "A New Cure for Headache": Mrs. Talmage Eglinton's maid Rosa (French); red lamp signals; she sneaks out to St Albans; Forsyth's letter via Ziegler (fake Duke letter).
Ch XVI "A Delicate Mission": Forsyth goes to Hotel Cecil as Duke's secretary; Benzon (Ziegler's secretary, the "Walcot" impostor); Mrs. T.E. confronts Forsyth at Kettner's ("very far from being indifferent").
Ch XVII "Where is the Duke?": Duke missing; Azimoolah says Duke took 7.30 to Tring, changes at Bletchley for North express to Liverpool.
Ch XVIII "The Senator and the Securities": Senator arrives Liverpool; mistakes Duke for con man; Duke takes him to muniment room safe.
Ch XIX "In the Crypt": Forsyth impersonates Duke with makeup; crypt meeting with Ziegler; packet is tissue paper; Ziegler pleads for it; Forsyth refuses; lets him go.
Ch XX "In the Muniment Room": Duke guards safe; Ziegler + Rosa + Benzon attempt; General, Senator, Forsyth, Sybil arrive; Azimoolah throws in Cora Lestrade's accomplice; Mrs. Talmage Eglinton = Cora Lestrade (ex-convict, Sing Sing) = Ziegler; Benzon escapes; Lestrade released.
Ch XXI "The Honor of the House": Duke confesses to Senator; Senator accepts his honesty; Duke to speak to Leonie. Epilogue six months later: Forsyth married Sybil in September; Duke & Duchess on honeymoon in Egypt; Cora Lestrade stabbed on train at Vienna; Standard paragraph; General's insight credited to Sybil.
